Vertex and edge centrality measures

centrality.Rd

Multi-threaded native C++23 implementations of classic network centrality measures matching graph-tool's centrality module: PageRank, Brandes vertex and edge betweenness, closeness (standard and harmonic), leading eigenvector centrality, Katz centrality, and Kleinberg HITS hubs and authorities.

Usage

pagerank(graph, damping = 0.85, pers = NULL, weights = NULL,
         tol = 1e-6, max_iter = 1000L)
betweenness(graph, weights = NULL, normalized = TRUE)
closeness(graph, weights = NULL, normalized = TRUE, harmonic = FALSE)
eigenvector_centrality(graph, weights = NULL, tol = 1e-6, max_iter = 1000L)
katz_centrality(graph, alpha = 0.01, beta = NULL, weights = NULL,
                normalized = TRUE, tol = 1e-6, max_iter = 1000L)
hits_centrality(graph, weights = NULL, tol = 1e-6, max_iter = 1000L)

Arguments

graph

An rgraphtool_graph object.

damping

PageRank damping factor in \([0, 1]\) (default 0.85).

pers

Optional non-negative personalization vector of length graph_num_vertices(graph).

weights

Optional edge property name or numeric vector of length graph_num_edges(graph). For betweenness() and closeness(), weights are interpreted as path lengths (distances); for spectral/walk centralities, weights are interpreted as connection strengths.

tol

Convergence tolerance for iterative power methods.

max_iter

Maximum number of power iterations.

normalized

Logical; whether to normalize centrality values.

harmonic

Logical; if TRUE, computes harmonic closeness \(\sum_{v \neq u} 1 / d(u, v)\) (divided by \(N - 1\) when normalized = TRUE).

alpha

Katz attenuation factor (should be smaller than \(1 / \lambda_{\max}\)).

beta

Optional exogenous vertex weight vector of length \(N\) for katz_centrality().

Value

pagerank(), closeness(), and katz_centrality() return numeric vectors of length \(N\). betweenness() returns a list with elements vertex (length \(N\)) and edge (length \(E\)). eigenvector_centrality() returns list(eigenvalue, vector), and hits_centrality() returns list(eigenvalue, authority, hub).

Examples

g <- graph_create(6L, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3), c(3, 1), c(3, 4), c(4, 5), c(5, 6), c(6, 4)))
pagerank(g)
#> [1] 0.1459854 0.1459854 0.2080292 0.2080292 0.1459854 0.1459854
#> attr(,"iterations")
#> [1] 8
betweenness(g)
#> $vertex
#> [1] 0.0 0.0 0.6 0.6 0.0 0.0
#> 
#> $edge
#> [1] 0.06666667 0.26666667 0.26666667 0.60000000 0.26666667 0.06666667 0.26666667
#> 
closeness(g)
#> [1] 0.5000000 0.5000000 0.7142857 0.7142857 0.5000000 0.5000000
